lede: A train pulling out of a station gains speed at a steady rate. Five quantities describe that: how fast it starts, how fast it ends, how quickly it changes, how far it goes and how long it takes. Four short formulae link them, and all four are printed on your Unit 2 sheet.
can: List $s$, $u$, $v$, $a$ and $t$, and fill in what you are given.
Choose the formula that leaves out the letter you neither have nor want.
Write the substitution line before rearranging.

text: Steady speeding up, in five letters

md: Five letters describe steady acceleration: $u$, $v$, $a$, $s$ and $t$. Each formula on the sheet holds four of them and leaves one out, so the choice is mechanical: fill in the three you are given, name the one you want, and take the formula that omits the letter you neither have nor need.

md: $s$ is the displacement, $u$ the velocity at the start, $v$ the velocity at the end, $a$ the acceleration and $t$ the time. Write the five out as a list at the start of every question and fill in what you are told. The list is the work; the formula is the easy part.

prompt: In the list $s$, $u$, $v$, $a$, $t$, which letter is the velocity at the start?
explain: $u$ is where the motion begins and $v$ is where it ends. Reading them the other way round turns most answers inside out.

alt: A table of the four constant-acceleration formulae with the letter each one leaves out: v = u + at leaves out s; s = half (u + v) t leaves out a; s = ut + half a t squared leaves out v; v squared = u squared + 2as leaves out t.
svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 354 210' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='354' height='210'><rect x='2' y='2' width='350' height='206' rx='8' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1' stroke-opacity='0.5'/><path d='M6 76H348M6 106H348M6 136H348M6 166H348M6 196H348M216 46V196' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='0.8' stroke-opacity='0.45'/><g fill='currentColor' font-family='inherit'><text x='12' y='35' font-size='13.5' font-weight='600'>Each formula leaves one letter out</text><text x='12' y='65' font-size='12' font-weight='600'>Formula (on the sheet)</text><text x='222' y='65' font-size='12' font-weight='600'>Leaves out</text><text x='12' y='95' font-size='13'>v = u + at</text><text x='222' y='95' font-size='13'>s</text><text x='12' y='125' font-size='13'>s = ½(u + v)t</text><text x='222' y='125' font-size='13'>a</text><text x='12' y='155' font-size='13'>s = ut + ½at²</text><text x='222' y='155' font-size='13'>v</text><text x='12' y='185' font-size='13'>v² = u² + 2as</text><text x='222' y='185' font-size='13'>t</text></g></svg>
caption: Each formula is missing one letter. Choose the one that misses the letter you neither have nor want.

md:
Each formula holds four of the five letters. Once your list shows three known values and one you want, that is four letters, and exactly one formula contains those four.

So the choice is never a guess: look at your list, find the letter that is neither given nor asked for, and pick the formula that leaves it out.

prompt: You know $u$, $v$ and $a$, and you want $s$. Which formula do you choose?
explain: The letter you neither have nor want is $t$, and $v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$ is the only one without it.

alt: A table matching phrases to values: speeding up at 2 metres per second squared gives a = 2; slowing down at 2 metres per second squared gives a = minus 2; starts from rest gives u = 0; comes to rest gives v = 0.
svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 374 210' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='374' height='210'><rect x='2' y='2' width='370' height='206' rx='8' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1' stroke-opacity='0.5'/><path d='M6 76H368M6 106H368M6 136H368M6 166H368M6 196H368M236 46V196' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='0.8' stroke-opacity='0.45'/><g fill='currentColor' font-family='inherit'><text x='12' y='35' font-size='13.5' font-weight='600'>Turning the words into signs</text><text x='12' y='65' font-size='12' font-weight='600'>The question says</text><text x='242' y='65' font-size='12' font-weight='600'>You write</text><text x='12' y='95' font-size='13'>speeding up at 2 m/s²</text><text x='242' y='95' font-size='13'>a = 2</text><text x='12' y='125' font-size='13'>slowing down at 2 m/s²</text><text x='242' y='125' font-size='13'>a = -2</text><text x='12' y='155' font-size='13'>starts from rest</text><text x='242' y='155' font-size='13'>u = 0</text><text x='12' y='185' font-size='13'>comes to rest</text><text x='242' y='185' font-size='13'>v = 0</text></g></svg>
caption: Four phrases that fill in a value for you.

md:
Take the direction of travel as positive. Then a body that is slowing down has a **negative** acceleration, because its velocity is falling. A deceleration of 2 m/s² goes into the formula as $a = -2$.

Two more phrases hand you a value: *starts from rest* means $u = 0$, and *comes to rest* means $v = 0$.

title: Why the sign matters so much
md: The sign is not decoration: it decides the answer. Put $a = 2.5$ where $a = -2.5$ belongs and a stopping distance comes out as $-80$ m. A negative distance or a negative time is almost always a sign that slipped.

prompt: A car travelling forwards decelerates at 1.2 m/s². What number goes in for $a$?
explain: Slowing down while travelling in the positive direction means the acceleration is negative, so $a = -1.2$.

alt: A straight line marked A and B, with 4 metres per second at A, 16 metres per second at B, and 8 seconds between them.

caption: A jet ski passes A at 4 m/s and B at 16 m/s, 8 seconds later.

md:
**List:** $u = 4$, $v = 16$, $t = 8$, and $a$ is wanted.
**Choose:** $s$ is neither given nor wanted, so use $v = u + at$.
**Substitute:** $16 = 4 + 8a$, so $8a = 12$ and $a = 1.5$ m/s².

For the distance AB, the list now shows $u$, $v$ and $t$, so $a$ is the spare letter: $s = \tfrac{1}{2}(4 + 16) \times 8 = 80$ m.

prompt: A body accelerates uniformly from 6 m/s to 14 m/s in 12 seconds. How far does it travel, in metres?
explain: $u$, $v$ and $t$ are known, so use $s = \tfrac{1}{2}(u + v)t$: half of $(6 + 14)$ is 10, and $10 \times 12 = 120$ m.

title: SUVAT The Equations of Constant Acceleration
why: Watch the list being written out before any formula is chosen. That order is what keeps long questions straight.

md: A question often walks you along one line through several points. Each stage has its own list, and the velocity at the middle point belongs to both: it is the $v$ of the first stage and the $u$ of the second.

prompt: You are short of time on a 2-mark part. What is worth writing first?
options: The formula with the numbers put in
answer: The formula with the numbers put in
explain: The substitution line carries the method mark (M). An unsupported answer earns nothing in Further Mathematics, even when it is right.

md: Nothing says a middle point is halfway. Its position comes out of the velocities, so work it out rather than assuming it.

prompt: A particle passes P, then Q, then R. For the stage from Q to R, what is $u$?
explain: Every stage starts where it starts. The velocity at Q ends the first stage and begins the second.

title: You can now
md:
List $s$, $u$, $v$, $a$, $t$ and fill in what you are given.
Choose the formula that leaves out the letter you neither have nor want.
Write a deceleration as a negative acceleration.
Square only the $t$ in the second term.
Carry a velocity from one stage into the next.

title: Sheet or memory?
md:
**Given on the Unit 2 sheet:** $v = u + at$, $v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$, $s = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$, $s = \tfrac{1}{2}(u + v)t$, the quadratic formula, $F = ma$, and the magnitude and angle of a vector.
**Must be known:** which formula leaves out which letter; that a deceleration is negative; that $g = 10$ m/s² when a question needs it.

prompt: Which of these is NOT printed on the Unit 2 formula sheet?
options: Which formula leaves out which letter
answer: Which formula leaves out which letter
explain: All four formulae are given. Knowing which one to reach for is the part that has to be in your head.

md:
List $s$, $u$, $v$, $a$ and $t$ for one stage of the motion.
Choose the formula that leaves out the letter you neither have nor want.
Write the substitution line before rearranging anything.
Take the direction of travel as positive and keep the signs.

One question of eight to ten marks in three or four parts, with follow-through all the way down. The first mark of each part is the list of values with the formula named; the last is the value with its unit. Stuck: write $s$, $u$, $v$, $a$ and $t$ with what you know beside them, because the list itself earns.
